author: reek
body: Alpha-to-coverage, shown as a split screen of alpha-cutout circles over a gradient. Left: one alpha sample per pixel, so the cutout edges are hard and jagged. Right: a 4x4 grid of coverage samples per pixel is averaged, so the same cutouts get smooth, anti-aliased edges -- what alpha-to-coverage buys you. One thread per pixel; the coverage fold is lowered to a WGSL loop. Reference site's "multisampling alpha to coverage" technique.

author: reek
body: 1 on a bar of a rotated fine grate, else 0 (the hard alpha test). Rotating the grid makes the thin diagonal bars a high-frequency alpha edge that aliases badly at one sample per pixel.
